# `silk/crypto/hkdf`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Derive keys with HKDF (RFC 5869) over SHA-256 or SHA-384.

## When to use
Use [`HkdfSha256`](#HkdfSha256) or [`HkdfSha384`](#HkdfSha384) to turn a shared secret, such as the result of an X25519
key exchange, into one or more keys of the length that you need. Give each key a different
`info` label so that the keys are independent.

## Details
HKDF has two steps. `extract` mixes the input key material with a salt and returns a
pseudorandom key (PRK) of one digest length. `expand` turns the PRK and an `info` label into
output of any length up to 255 digests: 8160 bytes for SHA-256, 12240 bytes for SHA-384. Nothing
allocates.

## Errors
- [`OutputTooLongError`](#OutputTooLongError) from `expand` if the output is longer than the maximum. The output does
  not change.

## Gotchas
HKDF is not for passwords. A password needs a slow function such as Argon2 or scrypt. The PRK is
a secret and is not erased.

## Examples
### Derive two keys from one secret
```silk
import silk.crypto.hkdf { HkdfSha256, OutputTooLongError }
import silk.core.result { Result }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let prk = HkdfSha256.extract(b"salt", b"shared secret")
  let mut encryption: [u8; 32] = [0; 32]
  let mut authentication: [u8; 32] = [0; 32]
  match HkdfSha256.expand(&prk, b"app v1 encryption", &mut encryption) {
    Result<(), OutputTooLongError>.Success { value: _ } => {}
    Result<(), OutputTooLongError>.Failure { error: _ } => {
      return 1
    }
  }
  match HkdfSha256.expand(&prk, b"app v1 authentication", &mut authentication) {
    Result<(), OutputTooLongError>.Success { value: _ } => {}
    Result<(), OutputTooLongError>.Failure { error: _ } => {
      return 1
    }
  }

  // Different labels give different keys.
  if encryption[0] == authentication[0] && encryption[1] == authentication[1] {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `HkdfSha256` with `import silk.crypto.hkdf { HkdfSha256 }`.

## `HkdfSha256`

```silk
pub struct HkdfSha256
```

HKDF with SHA-256 as the hash (RFC 5869). The PRK is 32 bytes and the output is at most 8160
bytes.

### When to use

Use it to turn a shared secret, such as the result of an X25519 key exchange, into one or more
keys of the length that you need. Give each key a different `info` label so that the keys are
independent.

### Details

HKDF has two steps. `extract` mixes the input key material with a salt and returns a
pseudorandom key (PRK). `expand` turns the PRK and an `info` label into output of any length up
to 8160 bytes. Nothing allocates.

### Gotchas

HKDF is not for passwords. A password needs a slow function such as Argon2 or scrypt. The PRK is
a secret and is not erased.

<a id="HkdfSha256.impl"></a>

## Implementation `HkdfSha256`

```silk
impl HkdfSha256
```

<a id="HkdfSha256.impl.extract"></a>

### Associated function `extract`

```silk
pub fn extract(salt: &[u8], ikm: &[u8]) -> [u8; 32]
```

Returns the 32-byte pseudorandom key (PRK) for the input key material `ikm` and `salt`.

An empty salt is the same as 32 zero bytes. Use a random salt if the protocol has one. Pass
the result to [`HkdfSha256.expand`](#HkdfSha256.impl.expand).

#### Gotchas
The program traps if `salt` or `ikm` is longer than the hash allows (2^64 bits).

<a id="HkdfSha256.impl.expand"></a>

### Associated function `expand`

```silk
pub fn expand(prk: &([u8; 32]), info: &[u8], output: &mut [u8]) -> Result<(), OutputTooLongError>
```

Fills all of `output` with key material from `prk` and the label `info`.

`prk` must come from [`HkdfSha256.extract`](#HkdfSha256.impl.extract), or be another uniformly random key of 32 bytes.
An empty `info` and an empty `output` are valid. The same `prk` and `info` always give the
same bytes, and a shorter output is a prefix of a longer one.

#### Errors
- [`OutputTooLongError`](#OutputTooLongError) if `output` is longer than 8160 bytes. `output` does not change.
